statement.text:
M. R. Vaughan-Lee and J. Wiegold (Proc. R. Soc. Edinburgh Sect. A, 95
(1983), 215–221) proved that if a finite p-group G is generated by elements of breadth
⩽ n (that is, having at most pn conjugates), then G is nilpotent of class ⩽ n2 + 1;
the bound for the class was later improved by A. Mann (J. Group Theory, 4, no. 3
(2001), 241–246) to ⩽ n2 − n + 1. Is there a linear bound for the class of G in terms
of n?                                                                 Ya. G. Berkovich
